e.etymology: A respelling of Easton, an English place name and surname meaning the settlement to the east.
As an Arabic name, a spelling of Zina, adornment or beauty. In English it has also been a short form of Zenobia, as with Zeena in Edith Wharton's Ethan Frome.
A phonetic spelling in the Alicia and Alesha family, favored in Puerto Rican families. Alicia is a Latinized form of Alice, from a Germanic name meaning of noble kind.
A modern elaboration of Laila, the Arabic name meaning night, with an added A-.
The Greek original of Theodore, from theos, god, and doron, gift. It is still the everyday form of the name in Greece.
An English place name and surname from Old English heorot, a hart or stag, and ford. Hartford, Connecticut, was named after Hertford in England.
A written abbreviation of Muhammad that is standard in Bangladesh and eastern India. It reaches US records when the short form is entered as the first name.
e.note: Reads as the abbreviation for a medical doctor or for Maryland; it is said aloud as Mohammad.

e.etymology: A Yiddish form of Shlomo, the Hebrew name of King Solomon, from shalom, peace. It is used mainly in Hasidic Jewish families.
A -yn spelling of Arden, an English surname and the name of the forest in Shakespeare's As You Like It. The place name goes back to a Celtic word for high.
A respelling of the English word life. The spelling was made familiar by R&B singer Lyfe Jennings in the mid-2000s.

e.meaning: son of the servant of St. John
e.etymology: A spelling of Macklin, a surname anglicized from Gaelic Mac Gille Eoin, son of the devotee of St. John.
From an Old Iranian word for a man or hero, the same element that ends the royal name Xerxes. Arshan is used in Iranian and South Asian families.
A form of the Hebrew name Uriah, joining ur, light, and a short form of the name of God. In modern Israel the related Oriya is given to girls as well as boys.
Arabic khalifa, one who succeeds or stands in for another. It is the word behind caliph, the title of the leaders who followed the Prophet Muhammad.
e.note: Best known in the US as the stage surname of rapper Wiz Khalifa and media personality Mia Khalifa.

e.etymology: A Punjabi Sikh name. The ending -leen means absorbed or immersed, as in Harleen and Jasleen.
A respelling of Cassius, a Roman family name of uncertain meaning, written to match its KASH-us pronunciation and the nickname Kash.
An Igbo name from Nigeria, a sentence meaning my God and I go together. It is given to boys and girls.
In the United States a recent elaboration of Amira, the Arabic name meaning princess. Amiria is also the Maori form of Amelia.
A respelling of Swayze, an English surname that Americans know best from actor Patrick Swayze.

assoc.t: Patrick Swayze, star of Dirty Dancing and Ghost

e.etymology: A recent coinage in the style of Hawaiian names ending in -lani, close to Delani and Kailani.
The name of the Oklahoma city, from Tallasi, old town in the Muscogee (Creek) language, a name the Creek people carried west from Alabama.
A spelling of Yaritza, a name from Mexico and the Spanish-speaking Caribbean. It rose in 2022 with singer Yahritza Martinez of the group Yahritza y Su Esencia.
The short form of Gregory, from Greek Gregorios, watchful. It was most popular as a full name in the United States in the 1950s and 1960s.
namesakes: Greg Brady (eldest son on The Brady Bunch)
Greg Heffley (hero of Diary of a Wimpy Kid)

e.etymology: A spelling of Dana that makes the long A plain. Dana began as an English surname, often explained as meaning a Dane.
An English surname from the many places called Newton, Old English for new settlement. It was a fairly common American first name in the 1800s.

assoc.t: Isaac Newton, physicist who described gravity

e.etymology: A respelling of Nathan, a Hebrew name meaning he gave. Nathan is the prophet who advised King David.
The Italian form of Henry, from the Germanic name Heimirich, which joins the words for home and ruler.
namesakes: Enrico Fermi (physicist who built the first nuclear reactor)

e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian form of Arnold, a Germanic name joining the words for eagle and power.
A spelling of Francesca that writes the Italian c the way it sounds. Francesca is the feminine of Francesco, from Late Latin Franciscus, a Frank or Frenchman.
A spelling of Dane, an English surname most often explained as a name for a person from Denmark.
An American form of the biblical Mahlah or Mahalath, Hebrew names borne by several women in the Old Testament. It was most used in the 1800s.
